result.text: The Evanstonian is an upscale independent hotel.
When a guest calls room service at The Evanstonian, the room-service manager takes down the order.
She then submits an order ticket to the kitchen to begin preparing the food.
She also gives an order to the sommelier (i.e., the wine waiter) to fetch wine from the cellar and to prepare any other alcoholic beverages.
Eighty percent of room-service orders include wine or some other alcoholic beverage.
Finally, she assigns the order to the waiter.
While the kitchen and the sommelier are doing their tasks, the waiter readies a cart (i.e., puts a tablecloth on the cart and gathers silverware).
The waiter is also responsible for nonalcoholic drinks.
Once the food, wine, and cart are ready, the waiter delivers it to the guest's room.
After returning to the room-service station, the waiter debits the guest's account.
The waiter may wait to do the billing if he has another order to prepare or deliver.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Model performer information only when responsibility is stated. Prefer lanes for ordinary organizational responsibility.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

result.rule: When the description identifies the object or information entity acted on by an activity: Label the corresponding BPMN activity using that stated entity rather than substituting a related but distinct one.

When the description states an activity and lists multiple purposes or criteria for it: Label the corresponding task with the core activity and its stated object; do not narrow the label to just one of the listed purposes or criteria.

When the description gives an activity together with contextual or implementation details: label the corresponding BPMN element with its core action and object, omitting details that do not distinguish the activity.

When the description assigns an action to a particular participant or distinguishes that action from related actions: label each corresponding BPMN element with the described action and responsible participant; do not substitute another actor or conflate it with a separate action
